headword: {燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}

definitions.gloss: refueling; fuel supply; act of supplying fuel to a vehicle, aircraft, or ship
definitions.explanation: Supplying fuel — gasoline, jet fuel, bunker oil, and so on — to a vehicle or vessel. Common in aviation, shipping, military, and road-transport contexts. The word can also be used metaphorically for refilling other "reserves."

examples.japanese: {飛行機|ひこうき}は{燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}のため{着陸|ちゃくりく}した。
{艦船|かんせん}への{燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}は{海上|かいじょう}でも{可能|かのう}だ。
examples.english: Refueling ships is possible even at sea.

examples.japanese: {長距離|ちょうきょり}トラックの{運転手|うんてんしゅ}は、{決|き}まった{サービスエリア|さーびすえりあ}で{燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: Long-haul truck drivers refuel at designated service areas.

notes:
Compound of {燃料|ねんりょう} (fuel) and {補給|ほきゅう} (replenishment, supply). It behaves as a noun and often takes する to form a verb ({燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}する, "to refuel"). Register is neutral-formal and the word is standard in news, military reporting, and technical writing; in casual speech speakers are more likely to say {給油|きゅうゆ} for cars at a gas station.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}する: to refuel
- {燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}を{行|おこな}う: to carry out refueling
- {空中|くうちゅう}{燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}: in-flight refueling
- {燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}{基地|きち}: refueling base
- {燃料補給|ねんりょうほきゅう}{機|き}: refueling aircraft (tanker plane)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {給油|きゅうゆ}: refueling (with oil or gasoline) — the everyday word for filling up a car
- {補給|ほきゅう}: replenishment, resupply — general term, not limited to fuel
- {ガソリン|がそりん}を{入|い}れる: to put in gas — the most casual conversational phrasing
- {満|まん}タン: full tank — casual; what you ask for at a gas station
